today.title: Medications today

companion.title: Medication helper
companion.subtitle: Short, plain answers about purpose, timing, and basic interaction cautions. Tap Read aloud on any reply. This does not replace your doctor or pharmacist.
companion.placeholder: Type your question… (or use dictation on your keyboard)
companion.suggested2: Why take this pill after food?
companion.suggested3: Can aspirin mix with my blood thinner?
companion.disclaimer: Information may be incomplete. For new symptoms, dosing changes, or emergencies, contact your care team right away.
companion.errorAssistant: Something went wrong reaching MedBuddy. Check your network and API settings, then try again.
companion.mockGeneric:
Purpose: many daily medicines support long‑term conditions like blood pressure or blood sugar. Timing often matches food or sleep so the body absorbs meds evenly and side effects are milder—your prescriber sets the exact plan.

Interactions: always tell your pharmacist everything you take, including OTC pills and herbs. This demo uses sample wording when the app is offline.
companion.mockDrugDetail:
Purpose: this type of medicine is commonly used for the condition on your label—for example steadying blood sugar or blood pressure.

Timing: «with meals» often helps stomach comfort or matches how the drug works through the day; «once daily at night» might fit how long the dose lasts. Follow the instructions on your bottle unless your clinician told you otherwise.

Cautions: some combinations (other prescriptions, pain relievers, or supplements) need a pharmacist review—ask before adding anything new.
companion.mockInteraction:
When two or more drugs overlap, the main risks are extra drowsiness, bleeding, kidney stress, or one drug changing the level of another.

Do not start or stop medicines on your own. Bring your full list (including over‑the‑counter) to a pharmacist or doctor visit so they can check pairings safely.

medications.title: My medications
medications.subtitle: All your medicines in one place—dose, how often, and how many you have left. Tap Listen to hear what each one is for. At the bottom, save questions and personal notes (like side effects) by voice or text. Editing the list will be available later.
medications.sampleExplanation: Take this medicine after meals to help control blood sugar and reduce stomach upset. If you feel nauseous, tell your family or doctor—do not stop on your own.
medications.sampleBpExplanation: Take this medicine after meals to lower blood pressure and reduce stomach discomfort. Take it at the same times each day; if you forget, do not double the next dose.
medications.sampleStatinExplanation: Take this medicine as directed to lower cholesterol and help protect your heart. If you have unusual muscle pain, tell your doctor—do not stop on your own.
medications.questionsSubtitle: Tell your doctor or pharmacist what you need: questions about your medicines, or notes about your body—like stomach pain, dizziness, or poor sleep after taking a pill. Speaking is easiest; you can also write below.

family.title: Family & care
family.body: Many older adults already use LINE every day for voice chats with family—no new app to learn. MedBuddy works on LINE too: send text or voice. Here you can invite family to share your log (backend coming soon).

modal.title: MedBuddy & LINE
modal.tagline: The LINE you already use is the front door—no new username or password.
modal.p1: We chose LINE because many older adults in Taiwan already open it daily; voice chat is familiar, so there is little to relearn.
modal.p2: LINE provides a Messaging API: each message to our official account is sent securely to our servers. We verify every webhook with your channel secret (HMAC-SHA256) before handling it.
modal.p3: LINE provides identity: each user has a stable line_user_id for our channel—that is how we recognize you, with no separate login. When someone new follows the bot, we create a user record and start onboarding.
modal.p4: Reply vs push: replies to user-initiated messages are unlimited. Push messages (reminders, carer alerts) count against monthly quotas; the free tier is tight for production, but paid plans are affordable for pilots. Where possible we use chat-initiated patterns (e.g., when you open LINE) so reminders are sent as replies, not pushes.
modal.p5: This mobile app is a companion UI; the same voice-first, low-friction idea applies as on LINE.
